newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES QUOTED STABLE TO FIRMER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES QUOTED STABLE TO FIRMER.

text.p: Short term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted stable to firmer on Wednesday in a market dealers said was "a little bit short" after settlement with the central Reserve Bank.
"The market is a little bit short, all the surplus we had before settlement has gone towards treasury bills which everyone is now trying to re-sell to get money," one dealer said.
He said discount houses were purchasing 91-day treasury bills from the central bank at 19 percent and re-selling them in the market at 18.85 percent, the same rates quoted on Tuesday.
Negotiable certificates of deposit with maturity of 30, 60 and 90 days were buying firmer at 21 percent from 20.50 percent and their selling rate also edged up to 19.25 from 19 percent.
Bankers acceptance bills were being bought unchanged at 19.50 percent but sold firmer at 19 percent from 18.85 percent across the board.
Call money held steady at Tuesday's 19 percent with the Reserve Bank indicating a pre-settlement market surplus of Z$202.1 million compared to Z$442 million the previous day.
